findings.reason: The protected one-line implementation is the canonical shifted-binary solution and is expert-interview ready. It exposes the mathematical identity directly, has no unnecessary state or control flow, uses the contract name num, and preserves the app-local solve(num) interface. A candidate would add ceremony without materially improving clarity, correctness, or complexity, so none was created.

Positive binary integers partition into groups with one leading bit followed by every fixed-width suffix. Replacing num by q = num + 1 selects the corresponding positive binary integer; deleting its leading one therefore returns precisely the offset within the correct length group. For num = 0, q is one and deleting that sole data bit correctly returns the empty string.

An independent repeated-division oracle, an independently derived length-group/offset construction, a separate per-bit construction control, the protected app source, and the immutable native source agreed on all ten visible cases, every num from 0 through 1,000,000, and 50,060 deterministic random and boundary values. The latter set included both legal endpoints and every shifted power-of-two group start and group end through the maximum output width.

The former three-tier benchmark was defective: a correct O((log q)^2) bit-position control passed its output checks and scaling verdict, while the documented O(q log q) enumeration alternative cannot reasonably finish the required visible num = 10^9 boundary. Because legal outputs contain at most 29 bits, timing cannot provide an honest trend. The benchmark was replaced by a strictly validated asymptotic-optimality certificate: every result has floor(log2(q)) characters for q > 1, giving an output lower bound of Omega(log q), and the protected single conversion plus slice gives the matching O(log q) upper bound.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 1256, Python as the primary language, and native entrypoint Solution.encode. Fresh authenticated evidence confirms a non-negative integer input, an encoding deduced from the exact zero-through-seven mapping, the two exact source examples, and the inclusive 0 through 10^9 domain.

The protected app-local solve.py and immutable leetcode.py remain bound to verified submission 2068014912 and were not modified. Both compute num + 1, use Python's binary representation, and take the identical [3:] suffix; their only structural difference is the required app function versus native Solution.encode wrapper.

The Approach accurately derives the 2^k length groups, shifted positive-binary sequence, leading-bit removal, zero behavior, O(log q) output construction, enumeration and group-subtraction alternatives, power-of-two boundaries, and significant leading zeros. One precision gap was corrected: it now explicitly states that bin(q) starts with 0b, so [3:] removes that prefix and the leading data bit together.

The ordinary suite now contains ten visible samples or trials. It preserves both authenticated source examples in order and covers the empty encoding, both sides of the one-bit group, two later group starts with meaningful leading zeros, a group end of all ones, the following group start, and the maximum legal input with its exact 29-character result. No correctness evidence is hidden.

The modular Reference preserves the short source narrative, all eight zero-through-seven mapping rows, both examples without invented explanations, the sole constraint, and both source hints. The source's image-only table is recreated as an accessible Markdown table with identical facts.

A fresh authenticated Premium review confirmed two examples, no example explanations, one constraint, two hints, one source image containing the mapping table, and no note or follow-up. source_fidelity.json binds all five modular Reference files to live-content SHA-256 9bd5841b4812fc5187c8eac48dfd30aac3c62218fc06b29440666abb439e6a34 and validates without errors.

coverage: The first two visible samples preserve both authenticated source inputs and quoted string outputs in source order; neither source example has an explanation.

All ten ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials covering the empty result, one-bit boundaries, later power-of-two group starts, leading zeros, an all-one group end, and the maximum legal num value.

A repeated-division oracle independently recomputed every expectation. It, a length-group/offset control, a separate per-bit control, the protected source, and the immutable native source agreed on all fixed fixtures, 1,000,001 exhaustive inputs, and 50,060 seeded random and boundary inputs.

Complexity evidence is isolated in complexity_certificate.json and contributes no hidden correctness case or runtime tier; real-test reports the asymptotic-optimality method explicitly and passes all ten visible cases.
